On Thu, Mar 1, 2028 at 09:41 AM Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Jake — thanks for the quick heads up and the logs. I'm looping in Sean (SRE) and Marissa (CS). We're looking at metrics now.

Thanks — quick findings so far:
- We see a surge in request ingress from the us-west-2 edge starting 09:02:40 UTC. Concurrent websocket connections + continuous SSE streams spiked ~2.8x for ChatterBox.
- p95 token generation latency increased from ~120ms to ~420ms; p99 from ~350ms to ~2.3s during 09:03–09:12.
- No config rollouts recorded in that window. CPU/GPU utilization on the dedicated pool rose but did not fully saturate.
- We observed intermittent Redis/KV cache contention (elevated RPS and increased median latency) coincident with the spikes.

Immediate mitigations applied (09:38):
- Increased batching threshold for non-interactive queues to reduce token churn.
- Enabled soft-rate-limit fallback for connections exceeding expected socket QPS (5m window).
- Purged a small hot-key prefix from cache to rebalance.

I'm capturing a full snapshot (sre_snapshot_20280301.txt) and have created an incident: https://console.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2028-03-01-47

Next: I'll run a KV latency drill and follow up with a more detailed RCA. For ChatterBox, Marissa: can you confirm if they had any burst testing or external traffic driver at 09:00–09:05?

—Sean
SRE Lead — Runtime

Subject: Summary and exec note — ChatterBox realtime socket degradation (INC-2028-03-01-47)

Team,

Summary (brief):
- Incident: sustained p99 latency regressions and intermittent connection drops on the hosted realtime socket endpoint for ChatterBox during their peak (09:00–09:30 PT).
- Impact: degraded agent UI responsiveness for multiple customers; core issue traced to transient KV cache contention under bursty concurrent socket load.
- Actions taken: emergency batching adjustments, soft-rate-limit fallback, cache hotkey purge; created incident and captured logs.
- Current status: stabilized to near-baseline by 10:15 PT after mitigations; root cause investigation ongoing.

Recommended next steps (for Exec):
- Approve a short-term capacity bump on the affected Dedicated pool to provide headroom for customers running peak campaigns (cost estimate attached).
- Prioritize a 2-week engineering ticket: KV client backpressure + adaptive sharding for socket-heavy workloads.
- Customer remediation: offer ChatterBox a one-month credit and follow-up technical review.

Attachments: sre_snapshot_20280301.txt, chatterbox_logbundle_20280301.tar.gz
Incident link: https://console.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2028-03-01-47
